9701-8.3.1.motivate: A reaction may be slow even when its products are energetically favourable. A catalyst changes how the reactants reach those products, making a lower energy route available.
9701-8.3.1.establish: A catalyst is a substance that increases reaction rate by providing an alternative mechanism of lower activation energy, and is chemically unchanged at the end. Catalysis is this catalytic increase in rate. At fixed temperature the Boltzmann distribution itself stays the same; the lower activation-energy threshold leaves a larger area under the curve to its right, so more particles have sufficient energy to react. On an energy against reaction pathway diagram, show catalysed and uncatalysed paths from the same reactant level to the same product level. The catalysed route has a lower barrier, but the overall enthalpy change is unchanged. Measure a forward barrier from the reactants and a reverse barrier from the products, using the peak of the step specified. Homogeneous catalysis has catalyst and reactants in the same phase; heterogeneous catalysis has them in different phases. A catalyst may enter intermediate steps but is regenerated by the end of the sequence.
9701-8.3.1.connect: Activation energy from 8.2 is the threshold to compare with the Boltzmann distribution. Reaction pathway diagrams from 5.1 show why a changed route can lower that threshold while keeping the same enthalpy change.
9701-8.3.1.note:
- Catalyst: alternative mechanism, lower activation energy, unchanged at the end.
- Fixed-temperature Boltzmann curve stays fixed; more particles exceed the lower threshold.
- Draw both paths with the same endpoints and different peak heights.
- Homogeneous: same phase; heterogeneous: different phases.
9701-8.3.1.self_explain: At fixed temperature, explain why adding a catalyst increases the fraction of particles able to react without changing the Boltzmann curve.

discover.stem: At a fixed temperature, what changes when an effective catalyst is added?
discover.explanation: The catalyst offers a lower-energy mechanism. The distribution and endpoint energies remain the same.
